newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid agencies prepare for pullout in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies prepare for pullout in Zaire.

text.p: Aid agencies in the east Zaire city of Goma, centre for refugee relief operations, are preparing for a partial or total evacuation by road, an aid worker said on Thursday.
"Aid agencies have been told to prepare for a 70 to 100 percent evacuation from Goma," said Steve Pratt of Care International by telephone from Goma, just across the border in Zaire.

"This would take place by road to the south to Rwanda. We have been told to stay put in our houses until the decision is taken," said Pratt. Other international aid workers said they were also restricted to their homes or offices in Goma city.

Heavy fighting has raged since early on Thursday on the outskirts of Goma between the Zairean army and Tutsi rebels pushing towards the airport from the north as more than 115,000 refugees trek west of the city after abandoning their camp.

Goma is the administrative centre for international relief operations to feed 1.1 million Rwandan Hutu refugees in camps inside Zaire as well as an estimated 200,000 Burundians and thousands of Zaireans uprooted by nearly two weeks of fighting.
A pull-out by aid agencies would leave the refugees, in close proximity to hostile Tutsi forces, without any obvious means of support. But the Rwandans have so far resisted fleeing back to Rwanda.
The Rwandan Hutus fled their homeland in 1994 during the genocide by Hutu forces of up to one million Tutsis and Hutu political moderates. They say they fear reprisals if they go home.
Aid agencies have been struggling to feed the refugees and improve hygiene in the huge camps, including Mugunga which already has some 400,000 residents and is the largest refugee camp in the world.

Paul Stromberg, a spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in the Rwandan capital Kigali, said on Thursday he believed the Tutsi rebels were deliberating striking at all aid routes to cut supplies to the refugees.
"It seems to be their strategy to cut supply lines for the refugees.
"The roads (to Goma) have been impassable since October 20 and yesterday the World Food Programme announced they would fly food into Goma today. And today the airport is attacked," he said.
"It appears not to be a mere coincidence," he added.
He said an estimated 20,000 Zaireans were moving with the population of Kahindo camp, which emptied earlier on Thursday, and 7,000 people had crossed into Uganda from Zaire between October 25 and 29.
